methods.image_display_scale: Up to 960px Commons source-hosted previews for reviewed files; original-pixel inspection NOT performed

visually_reviewed.subject: Ornate suspended silver-coloured sanctuary lamp, chains and building interior.
visually_reviewed.rationale: No recognisable red glass; museum-quality Catholic context, but user expects recognisable red sanctuary lamp. High ISO 8000 in EXIF implies original texture verification needed; do not treat as neutral studio object.

visually_reviewed.subject: Frontal close-up of white stone altar-rail balusters against dark background.
visually_reviewed.rationale: Only architectural detail; cannot teach complete communion rail or its gate. Original source identity accurate.

visually_reviewed.subject: Complete nineteenth-century French high altar, central Eucharistic tabernacle and six identifiable matching gilded candlesticks.
visually_reviewed.rationale: Credible preconciliar-type altar. Metadata explicitly counts SIX candlesticks. One source is reusable as AL01 context and AL07 annotated ensemble only; AL19 independent retable remains unproven. No new image counts for multiple object IDs.

visually_reviewed.subject: Marble Catholic tabernacle with white domed upper enclosure and large purple veil hiding its door; four altar candles surround it.
visually_reviewed.rationale: Correct liturgical furnishing, but veil and four additional candlesticks prevent a clear full-object teaching portrait. Consider AL05 secondary context.

visually_reviewed.subject: Single altar candlestick with one taper candle in ornate architectural background.
visually_reviewed.rationale: Canonical AL08 calls for individual altar candle, not candlestick. This photo better illustrates holder/candle in use.

visually_reviewed.subject: Complete authentic Mass wine cruet on reflective museum platform, other silver vessels and glass case visible.
visually_reviewed.rationale: Historically V letter implies vinum (museum says suggests, not a proof). Image contains other prominent museum objects; do not count as clean isolated hero.

visually_reviewed.subject: Entire nineteenth-century gilt/enamel altar bell standing upright with defined handle and blue decoration. Museum background and reflective base visible but out of focus.
visually_reviewed.rationale: Strongest near-term physical pilot subject; correct French Catholic liturgical provenance. Source preview supports composition but glare/noise at original resolution still untested.

visually_reviewed.subject: Three-tiered altar bell stack on steps in modern St Mel's Catholic Cathedral, Longford, Ireland.
visually_reviewed.rationale: More familiar modern altar bell geometry, but floor/steps context and restored modern cathedral make it a secondary in-use example, not a better isolated object than Carcassonne.
